art.title: Sunflowers
art.credit: Public domain · image via Wikimedia Commons
art.story: In the summer of 1888 Van Gogh was waiting in Arles for his friend Paul Gauguin, and painted sunflowers to decorate the guest room. He worked fast, before the flowers wilted: fifteen of them in a vase on a table, some fresh and bright with petals like flames, some already dropping their seeds on drooping stems. It is yellow on yellow on yellow, a daring idea at the time. He was proud of it and signed it on the vase, simply: Vincent.
